title: Filipino Myths: Creatures of the Night — Part 1
titleOptions: Filipino Myths: Creatures of the Night — Part 1
The Bakunawa and the Monsters of Filipino Mythology
Creatures Our Lolos and Lolas Warned Us About
hook: Long ago, a serpent rose from the sea to swallow the seven moons — and an entire nation grabbed their pots and pans to fight it. Tonight, we meet the creatures of the Filipino night.

scenes.text: Picture a night sky with seven moons shining over the Philippine islands — and a giant serpent in the sea, rising to swallow them one by one. That is where our story begins. Sapagkat sa mundong ito, ang dilim ay may mga ngipin. Because in the old Philippines, the darkness had teeth.

scenes.text: The Bakunawa was a moon-eating serpent of Visayan and Bicolano legend, so vast it could coil around the sea itself. Ayon sa matatanda, gutom na gutom ito sa liwanag. The old people said it hungered for light, and above all, it hungered for the moons.

scenes.text: In the beginning, Bathala placed seven moons in the sky, one for each night of the week, and the islands glowed silver after dark. Pero isa-isa silang nilamon ng Bakunawa, hanggang isa na lang ang natira. But one by one, the serpent rose from the deep and swallowed them, until only a single moon remained.

scenes.text: The kapre is less a monster than a guardian spirit of the old trees — which is why elders warn against cutting down a balete without permission. Humingi ka muna ng paalam sa puno. Ask the tree's leave first. Some of our oldest neighbors, after all, are still living in them.

scenes.text: The smallest creature in our story may be the easiest to offend. The dwende are tiny old men who live in earthen mounds and ant hills. May puting dwende na mabait, at itim na dwende na mapanakit. There are white dwende who bring luck — and black dwende who bring sickness.

scenes.text: But the tiyanak is no baby. The old tales say it is the spirit of a child who died unbaptized, or something far older wearing a baby's shape. Kapag binuhat mo ito, doon nagpapakita ang tunay nitong anyo. Once you pick it up, it shows its true face — claws, fangs, and laughter.

scenes.text: Seven moons, a flying woman, a neighbor who is not what he seems — these stories survived five hundred years of colonization, war, and smartphones. Dahil hindi sila basta kwento lamang — sila ay alaala ng ating mga ninuno. Because they were never just stories. They taught children where the dangers were, and taught everyone else to respect the dark.
